purpose: Specify the Unix PTY system seam with bounded child and terminal observations.
behavior: Checks master/slave close-on-exec flags, terminal identity, requested size and bidirectional bytes including CRLF echo translation.
Checks resize from 80 by 24 to 120 by 40 and the 1 by 32767 boundary.
Forks async-signal-safe-only child closures: a new session with make_controlling must receive SIGINT from typed Ctrl-C, while the unwired control reads past it; a non-session-leader must get EPERM.
contracts: Wait helpers impose a ten-second bound and drain PTY output while observing child exit, including the documented macOS exit dependency.
dependencies: pty_unix open/resize/make_controlling seam; libc terminal ioctls, fork and waitpid.
failures_or_limits: The helper kills a timed-out child before failing; assertions were inspected, not executed, so these platform conditions remain unverified here.

purpose: Own Windows ConPTY creation, resize and asynchronous close without blocking the supervisor owner.
behavior: Starts a dedicated closer before allocating the console, creates noninheritable pipes, calls CreatePseudoConsole with flags zero, and immediately closes PTY-side copies.
Sends the HPCON to the closer; dropping ConPty disconnects its channel so ClosePseudoConsole runs only on that thread.
Accepts dimensions 1 through 32767 and unwraps Win32 HRESULT codes into I/O errors.
contracts: The host receives input/output handles; CreateProcessW attributes and null standard handles belong to windows/spawn and create.
dependencies: windows/tree.rs must enforce stop deadlines independently; Windows Console APIs implement the OS boundary.
failures_or_limits: close(deadline) deliberately ignores its argument after transfer to Drop: it does not itself enforce a deadline. A failed send to the closer is ignored and would leave the pseudoconsole open; the code relies on the receiver remaining alive.

purpose: Bootstrap the Windows supervisor with host identity and lifetime watches before Ready.
behavior: Clears inherited ignore-Ctrl-C state, installs a supervisor-local console handler, opens a noninheritable host process handle and arms its wait thread.
Starts member tracking and diagnostics, connects to the named pipe and verifies its server PID, then starts channel workers and queues versioned Ready.
A generic watch helper waits on an owned process handle and posts the requested owner-loop event.
contracts: The host watch is armed before the channel or Ready; children inherit the cleared Ctrl-C ignore flag while the supervisor ignores console events.
dependencies: channel.rs verifies host PID and starts transport; members.rs tracks Jobs; queues.rs carries HostGone and root events.
failures_or_limits: Console handler call statuses and WaitForSingleObject return values are not checked; watch completion posts its event regardless of wait status. Process-handle ownership avoids watching solely by a later PID lookup.

purpose: Transport Windows host requests and replies on independently blocking overlapped pipe workers.
behavior: Opens the host named pipe without inheritance, with identification-only SQOS, and refuses a server PID different from --host-pid.
Decodes only Spawn, Go, Stop, Resize, List and Release; malformed input, wrong message direction or read failure posts HostGone.
One reader feeds the bounded Inbox and one writer drains Outbox frames; write failure closes output and posts HostGone, while completed writes signal owner progress.
Each side owns a manual-reset event and completes overlapped operations before dropping their buffers; ERROR_MORE_DATA remains readable partial data.
contracts: No synchronous pipe wait runs on the owner loop; queue bounds are supplied by queues.rs.
dependencies: omni_proto decode/encode framing; Windows named-pipe PID and overlapped APIs; boot.rs owns startup.
failures_or_limits: Helper threads use 64 KiB stacks and can remain inside OS I/O until the channel/peer ends; owner safety depends on queue stall enforcement elsewhere.

purpose: Build Windows executable, verbatim and batch command lines and decode protocol WTF-8.
behavior: Executable quoting preserves empty/spaced arguments and backslashes before quotes; argv[0] containing a quote is refused, while verbatim mode appends the tail unchanged.
Batch mode uses cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c, quotes metacharacters, defuses percent expansion, and rejects CR/LF arguments or percent-bearing script paths.

Removes a verbatim batch-path prefix only for equivalent drive/UNC spelling within its length check; WTF-8 decoding preserves lone surrogates but refuses NUL, overlong sequences and out-of-range code points.
Embedded tests specify std-derived quoting, raw-tail, batch-path and encoding cases.
contracts: The source attributes its quoting algorithm to a pinned Rust std commit and names deliberate refusal differences.
dependencies: windows/spawn.rs selects launch mode; std path absolute conversion verifies normalization equivalence.
failures_or_limits: General cmd shell syntax is intentionally exposed only through verbatim tails. The original prefixed path length is used for the conservative 260-unit check; port provenance and runtime argument recovery were not independently executed here.

purpose: Create AppContainer profiles and manage file grants, guarded DACL snapshots and restoration.
behavior: Read grants allow read/execute; write grants add write/delete but omit FILE_DELETE_CHILD. Existing explicit grants are reused, and revoke removes explicit entries for the SID.
Guard operations open the reparse point itself by handle; pin handles omit delete sharing, and volume/file-index identity deduplicates aliases.
Protect detaches DACL inheritance, revokes the profile rights and grants read/execute; capture stores DACL SDDL and restore reinstates its protected/unprotected state.
Profile creation reuses an existing profile SID; owned descriptors and converted ACL allocations are freed after use.
contracts: There are no deny grants; excluded paths must be kept outside granted trees or protected by guard handling.
dependencies: acl/dacl.rs handles named grant propagation; acl/sid.rs owns profile/capability SIDs; guard.rs coordinates snapshot lifetime.
failures_or_limits: The introductory deny-ACE behavior is a reported prior Windows observation, not verified here. Snapshot restoration is not a merge with unrelated concurrent ACL edits.
inference: External DACL changes during a guard lifetime could be overwritten when the captured snapshot is restored.

purpose: Read and update named-path DACLs for idempotent AppContainer grants.
behavior: Reads a security descriptor by path and owns its lifetime; a null DACL produces no matching explicit entries.
Enumerates only ordinary allowed/denied ACEs that are not inherited, matches SID equality, and recognizes an existing allow when its mask and inheritance flags cover the requested subset.
Merges an explicit access entry and writes through SetNamedSecurityInfoW so inherited ACEs propagate to an existing subtree.
contracts: Grant presence is an explicit-ACE check, distinct from calculating effective Windows access.
dependencies: acl.rs calls has/mentions/write for apply and revoke; Windows ACL APIs allocate descriptors and replacement ACLs.
failures_or_limits: Object-specific ACE forms and inherited entries are intentionally excluded from matching. Named-path grant writes do not use the reparse-point handle protection used for guards.

purpose: Own profile and custom-capability SIDs with the corresponding Windows allocation cleanup.
behavior: Distinguishes profile SIDs freed with FreeSid from capability SIDs freed with LocalFree.
Derives a named capability, frees all group SIDs and every extra capability SID, retains only the first, and errors if none is returned.
contracts: The raw SID remains valid only for the owning Sid lifetime; callers embed that pointer in security-capability and ACL structures.
dependencies: acl.rs creates profile SIDs; container/mod.rs requests the shared toolchain capability; DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName supplies allocations.
failures_or_limits: The comment describes the shared toolchain capability as adding no network service; actual access depends on Windows token checks and the grants maintained elsewhere. This module alone does not establish confinement.
